# Implementation Plan: HTML Hyperlink Support for Excalidraw Elements

---

## 1. Overview

Implement support for HTML hyperlinks in all Excalidraw element types (shapes and text), using markdown-style `[label](url)` syntax. Hyperlinks will be visually indicated by a blue underline on the canvas, be clickable (opening in a new tab), and links will be preserved in SVG and PDF exports.

---

## 3. Implementation Steps

### 3.1. Update Element Model

1. **Extend element types** (`packages/element/src/types.ts`, `excalidraw-app/src/types.ts`):
    ```ts
    export interface ExcalidrawElement {
      // existing fields...
      hyperlink?: {
        url: string;
        label: string;
      } | null;
    }
    ```
2. Update creation, update, and patch logic to handle `hyperlink`.

---

### 3.2. Markdown Link Parsing

1. **Create `parseMarkdownLink` utility** (`excalidraw-app/src/utils/parseMarkdownLink.ts`):
    ```ts
    export function parseMarkdownLink(text: string): { label: string; url: string } | null {
      const match = text.match(/^\[([^\]]+)\]\(([^)]+)\)$/);
      if (!match) return null;
      return { label: match[1], url: match[2] };
    }
    ```
2. **Integrate parsing in element text/label editing**:
    - On label/text change, detect `[label](url)` and set the `hyperlink` property.
    - Store only the label for rendering.

---

### 3.3. UI: Editing Hyperlinks

1. **Update element editing UI** (`ElementEditor.tsx`):
    - When a `[label](url)` is detected, show a hyperlink preview.
    - Provide a way to edit/remove the hyperlink from the element.
    - Show validation for well-formed URLs.

---

### 3.4. Canvas Rendering

1. **Update `ElementRenderer.tsx`**:
    - Render hyperlinked label using blue color (`#1976d2`) and underline.
    - For shapes: render the shape as usual, but if `element.hyperlink`, render its label as a blue-underlined hyperlink.
    - For text: render the text as a blue-underlined hyperlink if `hyperlink` is set.

    ```tsx
    // Pseudocode
    if (element.hyperlink) {
      <text
        style={{
          fill: "#1976d2",
          textDecoration: "underline",
          cursor: "pointer"
        }}
        onClick={() => window.open(element.hyperlink.url, "_blank", "noopener")}
      >
        {element.hyperlink.label}
      </text>
    }
    ```
2. **Add `HyperlinkOverlay.tsx`**:
    - Use an absolutely-positioned div overlaid on the canvas for clickable area.
    - On hover/click, show pointer, and open link in a new tab.

---

### 3.5. Interaction Handling

1. **Make hyperlinks interactive**:
    - On hover: show pointer, optionally tooltip with URL.
    - On click: open `element.hyperlink.url` in a new tab (`target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`).
    - Prevent default editing if clicking on hyperlink.

2. **Edge Cases**:
    - Ignore malformed markdown links (do not set hyperlink).
    - If only `[label]()` or `[](url)`, do not activate hyperlink.
    - Disable link if URL is not http(s).

---

### 3.6. Exports: SVG & PDF

1. **SVG Export (`export/svg.ts`)**:
    - For elements with hyperlinks, wrap text in `<a href="..." target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">`.
    - Ensure styling (blue underline) is preserved in SVG.

    ```xml
    <a xlink:href="https://example.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">
      <text fill="#1976d2" text-decoration="underline">Label</text>
    </a>
    ```

2. **PDF Export (`export/pdf.ts`)**:
    - Use PDF library's link annotation support to overlay clickable area for hyperlink text/shape.
    - Ensure correct coordinates for clickable region.

---

### 3.7. Validation & Error Handling

1. **URL validation**:
    - Allow all URLs, but only `http://` and `https://` are interactive.
    - In the UI, warn if the URL is malformed or unsupported.
2. **Graceful handling**:
    - Fallback to plain text if hyperlink parsing fails.
    - No crash on invalid markdown.

---

### 3.8. Testing

1. **Unit tests** (`element-hyperlink.test.tsx`):
    - Parsing markdown links (valid, invalid cases).
    - Rendering with/without hyperlink.
    - SVG and PDF export contain correct hyperlink markup.
    - Interactive behavior (open in new tab).

---

## 4. Technical Decisions

- Store hyperlink as a nullable `{ url, label }` field on each element.
- Only `[label](url)` at the root level of a label/text is parsed as a hyperlink (no inline/partial links).
- Use blue (`#1976d2`) and `underline` for visual indication, matching common hyperlink conventions.
- Use overlay divs for hit-testing/click handling to avoid interfering with drawing interactions.
- SVG links use `<a>` with `xlink:href`; PDF uses link annotations.
- Only `http(s)://` URLs are interactive; all URLs are preserved in exports.

---

## 5. Assumptions

- All shape and text elements can have a single hyperlink (no multiple/inline links per element).
- Hyperlink applies to the element's label/text, not shape geometry.
- Only `[label](url)` at the start/end of the text is parsed; no support for multiple links in one element.
- Export libraries for SVG/PDF support link embedding.
- No backward compatibility issues with existing elements (non-hyperlinked elements remain unaffected).
- The UI will not allow editing of the label and URL separately; users edit via markdown syntax.
- All updates must comply with existing project TypeScript/React/code style guidelines.

---
